why_angle: The cited Power Queen page and the other results give heater ratings and a 10 A trigger, but none says whether each heater runs only on charger current or can also warm the battery from its own stored energy. This page sorts each heated 12V 100Ah by heat source and adds the LiTime dual mode, Battle Born's heat-enable jumper and prices checked at the makers' stores today.
must: LiTime's LiHeat also pre-heats from its own stored energy

page.title: LiFePO4 Battery with Heater: Which 12V 100Ah Heats Without a Charger
page.h1: LiFePO4 battery with heater: what powers the heater, 12V 100Ah compared
page.desc: Heated 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 batteries: which ones heat only from charger current and which can pre-heat from their own energy. Maker prices checked 2026-11-13.
page.answer: Short answer. A heated LiFePO4 battery warms its cells with a built-in pad before it accepts charge below freezing. Pick the Redodo 12V 100Ah self heating (100 W pads, on below 32°F, off at 41°F) when a charger feeds it; LiTime's LiHeat also pre-heats from its own stored energy.
columns: What starts and stops the heater

cells.heater_source: 100 W dual pads, run while charging is on hold; no battery-powered pre-heat mode listed (Redodo)
cells.needs: Starts when cells drop below 32°F; stops at 41°F, then charging resumes (Redodo)

cells.heater_source: Charger, or the battery's own stored energy (dual mode, LiTime)
cells.needs: Heats automatically with a charger plugged in, or pre-heats from battery power before charging (LiTime)

cells.heater_source: Charger input, two heating pads (Freedom in a Can)
cells.needs: A charging source of at least 10 A; on below 41°F, off at 50°F (Freedom in a Can)

cells.heater_source: Charger input only: incoming charge power goes to heating, not the cells (Vatrer)
cells.needs: Charger connected at 32°F; heating stops and charging starts above 41°F (Vatrer)

cells.heater_source: The battery's own stored energy (Battle Born)
cells.needs: Jumper from positive terminal to the heat-enable post; on below about 35°F, off near 45°F (Battle Born)

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Pre-heat premium: $368.99 − $251.99 = $117 more for LiTime's mode that warms the battery from its own charge.
  • Charger share while heating: Redodo recommends its 14.6 V 20 A charger (14.6 × 20 = 292 W). The 100 W pads equal 100 ÷ 292 = 34% of that charger's output. On a 10 A charger (146 W), they equal 100 ÷ 146 = 68%.
  • Energy per warm-up: Redodo states 30–60 minutes from 14°F to 50°F for the 100 W heater, so 100 W × 0.5–1 h = 50–100 Wh, or about 4–8% of a 1,280 Wh battery (12.8 V × 100 Ah).
  • Battle Born cost: $999 ÷ 100 Ah = $9.99 per Ah, 9.99 ÷ 2.52 = 4.0× the Redodo's cost per Ah.

Charger-powered or self-powered: where the heat comes from

Below freezing, the BMS refuses charge current to protect the cells. LiTime explains that the 0 A a charger shows on a cold battery is often the BMS actively refusing the charge. A heater only solves this if it has power to run on, and the makers split into two designs.

Charger-powered. Vatrer states it plainly: when a charger is connected at 32°F, incoming charging power goes to heating instead of the cells, and charging starts above 41°F. Shari Galiardi (Freedom in a Can) tested Renogy's DuoHeat with a 20 A AC charger and a 50 A DC-DC/MPPT charger, and reports that it needs a charging source of at least 10 A. Redodo's 12V 100Ah page says charging halts until the pads raise the cells above 41°F, and it lists no battery-powered mode. Redodo describes an App Pre-Heat mode from stored energy only on its Apex Mini 24V. With a charger-powered heater, a weak winter panel that never reaches the heater's current floor leaves the battery cold and charge-locked.

Self-powered. LiTime's LiHeat can warm the battery while plugged in, or pre-heat it from battery power before charging. Battle Born's heater draws from the battery itself, but it will not turn on until the heat-enable post is jumpered to the positive terminal. In a multi-battery bank, the posts are chained and fed from the highest-voltage point. Battle Born suggests an inline switch so the heater does not drain the battery in storage. Its heater turns on below about 35°F, turns off near 45°F and allows charging above about 25°F. Battle Born says warming from freezing can take 2 to 4 hours.

Measured warm-up. Shari Galiardi froze a Renogy Core Mini DuoHeat four times, and each time it reached charging temperature in 11–20 minutes. Her single-pad Renogy 100Ah PRO took just over an hour. Redodo's own figure for its 100 W pads is 30–60 minutes from 14°F to 50°F. frater secessus quotes a REPT LFP cell datasheet that limits charging to 0.1C, up to 80% SOC, between 32°F and 50°F. Even after a heater shuts off at 41°F, a gentle charge rate is kinder to the cells.
